title: Puff Pastry Methods
description: Choose your fighter: traditional, rough puff, or store-bought — each has its own rewards.

traditional.instruction: Make the détrempe: mix flour, salt, and soft butter. Add ice water gradually to form a smooth dough. Wrap and chill 30 minutes.
Prepare butter block: pound cold butter between parchment paper into a 15 cm square. Chill until firm but pliable.
First lamination: roll dough into a cross, place butter block in centre, fold flaps over to enclose, roll into a rectangle.
Perform turns: fold in thirds like a letter, rotate 90°, roll and fold again. Repeat for 6 turns total, chilling 30 minutes between sets. Rest 1 hour before use.

rough_puff.instruction: Mix flour and salt. Add cold butter cubes and lightly rub in, leaving visible pea-sized pieces for flakiness.
Add ice water and mix until rough, shaggy dough forms. Do not overwork.
Roll dough into a rectangle on floured surface and fold in thirds. Wrap and chill 20 minutes.
Repeat rolling and folding for a total of 3–4 turns, chilling 20 minutes between turns. Final chill 30 minutes before use.

store_bought.instruction: Thaw frozen puff pastry sheets until just pliable but still cold, about 10–15 minutes.
Cut, shape, and bake according to your recipe. Ready-made puff pastry gives excellent results with zero prep stress.

notes.title: Temperature Control
notes.content: Keep everything cold. If butter softens too much, return dough to fridge. Cold butter ensures distinct layers and maximum flakiness.

notes.title: Traditional vs Rough Puff vs Store-Bought
notes.content: Traditional: ultimate rise and flakiness, 3+ hours. Rough puff: faster (≈1 hour), still good. Store-bought: instant, fully acceptable.

notes.title: Make Ahead
notes.content: Homemade puff pastry freezes well for up to 3 months. Wrap tightly in plastic wrap and foil; thaw overnight in the fridge before using.

notes.title: Choose Your Path
notes.content: Traditional = glory. Rough puff = smart compromise. Store-bought = practical and efficient. Pick according to time, ambition, and patience.
